Hardware-facing SDK matches must preserve synchronization and memory constraints visible in assembly: AX voice-stack mutations retain interrupt masking, while ARAM and auxiliary-buffer operations retain 32-byte alignment and explicit cache flush or invalidation.

When recovering static strings used by inline assertions, test ASCII decoding first; this is distinct from much of Melee's displayed gameplay text, which is represented through indexed texture data and SIS objects rather than a conventional text encoding.

statement: For matching HSD assertion expansions, preserve the original explicit source-line value instead of relying on __LINE__; using __LINE__ would otherwise require placing the reconstructed assertion on the original source line.

corroboration.reason: The __assert area anchor exists, and the cited Discord discussion supports retaining explicit assertion line values instead of substituting __LINE__. Existing assert standards are compatible with this clarification.

statement: Use tightly scoped push/force_active/pop pragma blocks when matching requires otherwise-unreferenced CARD functions to remain emitted.

When an assembly unit is replaced by C and gives anonymous data labels meaningful global names, update every still-assembly dependent to reference the named globals in the same change so incremental conversion remains linkable.

statement: Supply merged, relevant project PRs to coding agents as examples of accepted project-specific idioms and quirks, while controlling subagent breadth because broad historical comparisons can consume substantial tokens.

For agent-facing assembly diffs, inspect the full diff initially to establish context, then switch to a form that collapses matching lines during iteration to reduce token use without hiding the initial overall shape.

For file-wide agent decompilation, explicitly instruct the agent not to skip functions because of size and state any acceptable threshold for large functions; this reduced premature skipping in reported use.

Turn recurring decomp patterns into scripts and teach agents to invoke them; scripts provide guardrails and automate mechanical work such as include management, leaving the agent to focus on semantic and matching decisions.

For large or complex functions that stall an agent, first perform an understanding pass over callers, callees, surrounding code, likely signature, and high-level behavior. Correct partial documentation and runtime inspection can provide context that helps subsequent matching, but a human must validate the interpretation.

Raw MWCC diagnostic logs are difficult for agents to interpret reliably; structured extraction and presentation are needed, although a sufficiently capable agent can sometimes use the raw debugger output to resolve a register swap.
AI-assisted matching batches should be gated before review for raw offset pointer arithmetic, NOT_IMPLEMENTED-only bodies, C99 declaration-rule violations, and missing prototypes.

statement: For an empty wildcard output section such as `.text ALIGN(0x20):{}`, `mwldeppc` places contributing input sections according to the object order supplied on the linker command line. This ordering applies only within the matching output section: placing an object first cannot move its ordinary `.text` contribution into `.init`.

statement: When an asm-to-C migration exposes duplicated or section-sensitive strings whose placement prevents matching, isolate those data symbols in small aligned assembly objects instead of forcing unrelated C translation units to own them.

When relinking an assembly-backed object, update its object-style assembly, split ranges, build classification, and link-object lists together; for a NonMatching source range, keep only one of the source or assembly objects in the active link lists.

When splitting a monolithic assembly data object, place unresolved data in the assembly file for the module that owns its references while preserving labels, alignment, declarations, and raw contents; migrate only high-confidence declarations to C.

statement: Compiler-version matching corrections can be isolated in a post-compilation object-file transformation invoked by the generic C object build rule, avoiding source-level workaround constructs in every decompiled file.

With affected older CodeWarrior versions, defining an assembly function can disable peephole optimization for the remainder of the translation unit; restore the setting with `#pragma peephole on` or isolate the assembly-related pragma state with push/pop.

For CodeWarrior data placement, uninitialized objects normally map to .bss, initialized writable objects to .data, and initialized const objects to .rodata; corresponding small objects may instead use .sbss, .sdata, and .sdata2.

Apply CodeWarrior matching controls such as PAD_STACK, dont_inline pragmas, and helper call boundaries narrowly around affected functions; the movement and memory-card PRs used these local controls while producing substantial new matches without making them subsystem-wide conventions.

Incorrect constructor and destructor section alignment metadata can be repaired by locating .ctors and .dtors by name and changing their ELF section-header alignment field to 4.

When toolchain limitations prevent irregular characters in mangled C++ symbols, compilation-safe placeholders can be decoded in non-section-name ELF string tables after compilation, with in-place replacements length-checked and zero-padded.

Do not assume that commuting operands in a floating-point expression is universally codegen-neutral: it often preserves code generation, but an edge case can change register assignment and produce a register swap.

For CodeWarrior inline assembly copied from a standalone assembly file, an SDA-relative operand may need the explicit @sda21(r2) suffix removed; the inline assembler can otherwise reject the label use.

Do not treat CodeWarrior scheduling-on versus scheduling-off output as a guaranteed pure instruction permutation: disabling scheduling was observed to change register allocation, while other examined prologues retained their stack-frame instruction order and instead admitted main-body loads. Classify frame and body instructions explicitly and validate the model across multiple functions.

CodeWarrior linker-map parsers must account for more than one map layout, including an older form without a File offset column and a newer form with that column; progress-calculation failures should not automatically be attributed to symbol parsing.

statement: A data object's linkage can affect generated instructions and register allocation, so verify whether referenced data is file-local or external when resolving an otherwise unexplained match difference.

Move data into the C translation unit that owns it when reconstructing that unit; use an extern declaration when the data belongs to another unit. Treat extern-only stand-ins as provisional because they can produce code that does not match.

When converting raw small-data and data sections for shiftability, a script that emits `.4byte` entries from a specified offset and length can accelerate pointer-table extraction; jump tables can then be handled from the extracted entries.

For known data-section symbols whose initializers are not yet transcribed, prefer extern declarations over tentative uninitialized definitions; tentative definitions can place the symbols in BSS and shift subsequent static-data ordering, breaking otherwise matched functions.
Do not force uncertain regions out of incbins: reconstruct only the ranges whose exact boundaries and representation are established, leaving unresolved tables or blobs intact for a later pass.

corroboration.reason: PRs 89 and 90 support retaining uncertain binary ranges as incbins while reconstructing only established spans.

statement: Function-pointer table recovery may require exposing the referenced code-entry boundaries first, so data entries can use symbols instead of anonymous instruction addresses.

Automatically writing a permuter result back into the original source is not a straightforward textual patch when preprocessing expands macros; application may require an agent or another source-aware reconstruction step.

Treat a lower decomp-permuter score only as a lead: inspect the resulting assembly to identify which source region affected the target difference, because many nominally better candidates contain unrelated or genuinely worse assembly changes.

Treat permuter output as a candidate rather than clean final source: inspect it manually, remove unrelated retained mutations, and give surviving temporary variables descriptive names instead of leaving generic names such as new_var.

A source permuter cannot discover a solution that requires changing external declarations or layouts, such as a struct or an unprovided inline, and it does not exhaust every possible internal expression form; failure after many iterations therefore does not establish that the current function structure is correct.

Choose the permuter based on the remaining instruction-level differences rather than the displayed fuzzy percentage; register assignments, redundant moves, and independent instruction ordering are suitable signals even when the overall percentage is not especially high.

statement: When a compiler-generated unrolled copy loop obscures a higher-level struct copy, a decompiler can replace the verified loop with an explicit synthetic copy operation while retaining separate aligned and unaligned forms.
Pattern-based decompiler normalization should be narrowly constrained by architecture, compiler, instruction shape, and location rather than broadly rewriting superficially similar instructions.

Before feeding decompiler output to the compiler or permuter, replace '?' placeholder types with valid C declarations and ensure the intended, most recently saved function was exported; otherwise the tooling failure may come from stale or uncompilable input rather than the candidate function.

A Git synchronization helper that rewrites branch history should make its force-push behavior explicit; preserving local work with a preliminary commit and a soft reset does not remove the history-rewrite risk.

To diagnose shifted or reordered non-text data, compare the nonmatching DOL with the known-good DOL, use Ghidra to map mismatching expected bytes back to virtual addresses, inspect the generated map for where shifts begin, and compile the affected translation unit with -S to associate section bytes with labels.
For a build-tool flag cleanup, keep the artifact input, output, layout-related arguments, and post-generation checksum verification unchanged so the edit remains isolated from matching behavior.

When reconstructing source-file boundaries from a stripped DOL, use assertion filenames and naming consistency as filename evidence, then combine function-pointer grouping and distinctive data with trial-and-error to infer splits; these inferred names and boundaries are not equivalent to recovered symbol-map metadata.
When the linker omits usable physical addresses from ELF program headers, normalize the linked ELF before extracting its loadable segments into a DOL.

To isolate calls associated with a runtime transition in Dolphin Branch Watch, collect normal activity first, mark it as "code path not taken," perform the target transition, mark that interval as "code path was taken," then discard later activity with another "code path not taken" marker before saving the trace.

Fixed-address declarations shared by MWCC, decomp-permuter, and host compilers should hide compiler-specific placement syntax behind one conditional declaration-suffix abstraction: preserve MWCC colon-address syntax, map the permuter path to FIXEDADDR, and expand away for compilers without fixed-address syntax.

GX writes through WGPIPE are accesses to the memory-mapped graphics FIFO and must be represented as volatile; introducing the volatile FIFO representation reduced the examined function to a register swap and then produced a match.
Constant-pointer writes produced around GX operations may represent inlined GX functions; reconstruct them as inline-function expansions rather than assuming they originated as macros.

For fixed hardware addresses used by split-address PowerPC instructions, write the complete numeric address with @h/@l relocations instead of manually pairing a page constant with an unqualified low immediate.
When C declarations are included by a C++ translation unit, wrap them with C linkage guards to suppress C++ name mangling.

An include guard is ineffective when the macro tested by #ifndef differs from the macro introduced by #define; PR 167's _OS_H__ versus _OS_H_ pair therefore did not make the Dolphin OS header safe for repeated inclusion.
In Dolphin runtime sources, code whose availability depends on Metrowerks/Gekko inline assembly should be guarded by `MWERKS_GEKKO` rather than by the object's `MUST_MATCH` bookkeeping state.

statement: A related title's debug ELF can provide reusable symbol identities for shared Dolphin SDK and baselib code instead of relying on semantic guesses from local control flow.

In the affected Dolphin DSP and DVD files, original-binary artifacts needed by normal matching builds are guarded with #ifndef BUGFIX rather than #ifdef MUST_MATCH, so they remain present by default and are omitted only from bugfix builds.

When importing Dolphin SDK reference code, compare multiple dated SDK builds instead of assuming one release is uniformly closest. For HIO, the December 2001 debug implementation was substantially closer to Melee than the September 2001 material, with ExtHandler immediately matching.

Do not remove apparently unused source artifacts solely as cleanup when matching Dolphin SDK objects: an unused volatile DSP mailbox read, a force-active debug string, DVD .bss padding, and an unused OSGetArenaHi assignment were retained while the corresponding objects were promoted to Matching.

When reorganizing monolithic assembly, use linker-map or object-boundary evidence to create subsystem or object-oriented units, but retain coarse residual units where mixed-object boundaries remain uncertain.

A matching external debug ELF can resolve placeholder Dolphin SDK symbols without behavioral changes; PRs 498 and 500 used Zoids VS symbols to recover names that remain present in current Dolphin GX, DVD, and VI source units.

For shared Dolphin SDK or library routines, inspect implementations from related decompilation projects as a starting point, but expect to adapt them for version-specific code generation or behavior rather than copying them unchanged.

Proper Doxygen briefs and parameter documentation should use /** block comments and live in .dox files; .dox files should contain clean documented declarations without preprocessor commands or declaration-sorting address comments, and single-line documentation comments should not be added to C or header files.

statement: In Doxygen parameter documentation, ordinary input is the implicit default. Use [out] for pointed-to storage that the function supplies as a result without requiring prior initialization, and avoid treating every object pointer that may mutate internal state as an out parameter.

DSP mailbox helpers should preserve 16-bit volatile MMIO semantics: readiness comes from bit 15 of the mailbox status halfword, reads combine the high and low halfwords, and sends write the high halfword before the low halfword.

DTK object splits must keep each `extab` and `extabindex` entry in the same object as the function it describes; unexpected redistribution of those sections after adding a split is a warning that object boundaries need review.

statement: Binary-conversion tooling should receive an explicit target selector and gate target-specific program-header assumptions behind it, preserving the default target's behavior.

statement: A GX display list is a buffered copy of the command stream normally written to the GX FIFO. statement: When matching closely related item translation units, compare sibling implementations side by side and preserve their common control-flow and callback structure while substituting only item-specific constants such as effect and SFX IDs.
Use normalized single spacing in plain-English item identity comments; the reviewed form was `// Sheik chain`, not `// Sheik  chain`.

statement: When item logic accesses only a partially understood item-specific variable block, model the proven fields at their exact offsets, retain padding and offset-based names for unknown regions, and expose the layout through the shared item union rather than using raw-byte access.

At itGetKind comparison sites, use the corresponding named item-kind constant instead of a raw numeric value when the mapping is established; this preserves the comparison value while exposing its domain meaning across fighter, player, and stage code.

Reconstruct verified jump tables as ordered symbolic references to their case targets, adding labels at internal branch destinations so the table exposes control-flow structure without changing instructions.

The assembly ranges split by PR 75 at 0x8000E9F0 and 0x80028B9C correspond in the current tree to src/melee/lb/lbshadow.c beginning with lbShadow_8000E9F0 and src/melee/cm/camera.c beginning with Camera_80028B9C, respectively.

When reviewing the history of src/melee/lb/lbshadow.c or src/melee/cm/camera.c, PR 75's large add/delete assembly diff should be treated as object-boundary movement: the decisive evidence is the synchronized object-list ordering and the start addresses of the moved ranges, not the raw diff size.

Relinking a library can require coordinated changes beyond configure.py status updates: source declarations, include dependencies, matching pragmas, and remaining assembly object boundaries may all need adjustment in the same relink.

A behavior-backed function rename should be applied consistently across the symbol configuration, implementation declarations, and assembly and C callsites; PR 1161 coordinated this for lbArchive_LoadSections and lbArchive_LoadArchive.

statement: Prefer domain types over byte arrays or raw address arithmetic when size and member use support them; typed GXColor and mpLib records expose meaningful members while preserving the code shapes used by their callers.

statement: When collision-library functions are identified, propagate their current names through dependent C and assembly callsites in the same change; PR 724 replaced anonymous address-based calls across fighter, item, effect, map, and baselib code, while the current implementation remains anchored in `src/melee/lb/lbcollision.c` under `lbColl_*` symbols such as `lbColl_CopyHitCapsule`.

In legacy-C decompilation contexts, declare locals at the start of a block and provide complete function prototypes, including return types. Otherwise declarations after statements may be rejected, and an undeclared or return-type-less function may be treated as returning `int`, introducing spurious integer-to-float conversions.
When splitting one assembly blob into multiple objects, update the link configuration in the same change to preserve the original section and object order.
A shiftable build permits code and functions to be added or removed while the linker relocates references, reducing reliance on fixed pointers and manually managed free space.

GameCube data shiftability is more constrained than code shiftability because compiler-generated short section-relative references can tie data layout to a translation unit; full data shiftability may therefore require the affected unit to be fully decompiled.
A code split that changes linked object boundaries must update the project's link-order metadata in the same change so the final section layout remains stable.

When many pointer-valued diff entries all move by the same amount, first look for an earlier compiled region or alignment contribution whose size differs by that amount rather than debugging each pointer independently.

Before investigating an apparent linker-versus-game address discrepancy, verify that the map being inspected is the intended expected or matching-build map rather than a WIP map; in this case the discrepancy disappeared after identifying the wrong map file.

For a byte-matching build, a linker map generated from an OK build can translate original runtime addresses into current non-static symbols because the linked DOL preserves the original layout; static functions may not appear in the map.

When the linker command file defines and places the small-data memory regions correctly, the Metrowerks linker can generate the SDA and SDA2 base values; the experiments reported each base as its corresponding small-data region base plus `0x8000`.
Executable reconstruction must preserve the original section placement and PowerPC small-data bases; matching instruction text alone is insufficient to reproduce the binary layout.

In code-matching changes, keep ordinary string and float literals inline unless data-ownership evidence and the PR scope justify introducing symbols; address-style symbol substitutions in the affected files were rejected as less readable and were restored to literals.

Current LLM-assisted decompilation still requires human review and guardrails for validation, project conventions, C89 compliance, typed access, and avoidance of fakematches; concise subsystem-specific instructions with complete worked examples are more actionable than one large undifferentiated prompt.
For a local before-and-after overview of matching changes, run ninja baseline before editing and ninja changes_all afterward.

For stubborn long-tail matches, build tooling for one function first, test how far it generalizes, classify other functions that exhibit the same case, and apply it only to that class; this is slower than a broad pass but was reported to solve several resistant functions.
In Melee, Luigi's Super Jump Punch is his primary vertical recovery move, but it travels straight upward with no horizontal range; Green Missile and Luigi Cyclone provide his horizontal recovery.

Do not indiscriminately inject every file-local static-data header into a global m2c/decomp.me context: unrelated definitions can corrupt inferred data offsets. Prefer the static declarations relevant to the function's current source file, or make the global static-data block easy to disable.

Keep m2c valid-syntax placeholders and cross-compiler keyword shims centralized in shared headers, with compiler- and M2CTX-specific behavior hidden behind macros instead of repeated raw constructs in consumer headers.

Unknown-offset output such as `unk28` or M2C_FIELD is a context problem rather than suitable final source: add the correct parameter types and struct members to the decompiler context, then rerun m2c so it emits typed member access.

When an m2c context contains a symbolic array size that m2c will not expand, configure the context preprocessor to evaluate that specific macro before emitting the context while leaving the macro form in the project source.

corroboration.reason: The cited discussion consistently supports expanding a specific symbolic array-size macro in the generated m2c context without changing the project-source macro.

statement: Do not rely on preserved #ifdef branches to present different GObj types to m2c and MWCC in one generated context: m2c rejects preprocessor directives in its C context, so this requires preprocessing into separate views or upstream type-override support.

corroboration.reason: The cited discussion consistently reports that preserved preprocessor branches cannot provide separate m2c and MWCC type views in one m2c C context.

statement: For m2c-generated starting points, --valid-syntax generates M2C_FIELD while --no-casts reduces surrounding casts; the two options can be combined before recovering typed fields.

Remove explicit casts that convert an expression to the type it already has because they add visual noise; retain and investigate casts across genuinely different integer widths, such as long and int, because those can affect generated code.

When M2C reports an instruction such as mflr outside a function immediately after assembly was copied into a scratch, verify that the function label was copied too; restoring the omitted label resolved this failure in the reported case.

The project's .static.h headers are temporary m2c scaffolding used to expose static declarations to m2c; their declarations should be removed or moved into the source as the translation unit approaches completion.
Keep generated M2C context and candidate source artifacts out of version control while giving them distinct paths or suffixes that separate them from maintained decompilation source.

statement: When feeding m2c output into another decompilation pass, `--no-casts` can replace raw pointer arithmetic with M2C_FIELD placeholders, and `--union-field Type:member` can identify a known union arm; these options improve the intermediate representation but do not remove the need to recover proper typed fields before review.

When generating an m2ctx context, restricting the header list to the declarations and structures needed by the target substantially reduces parsing time; unused function-declaration headers can be omitted.

corroboration.reason: The two cited attempts support reducing m2ctx parsing work by limiting headers to required declarations and structures.

statement: For m2ctx context generation, the unmerged tactic of passing --passthru-magic-macros to pcpp should not be treated as the preferred fix without examining its replacement in PR 920; the author closed PR 919 and described that change as probably not the best solution.

statement: Linux context generation can retain the existing MWCC preprocessing pipeline by prefixing its command with Wine rather than changing compiler flags or substituting a different preprocessor.

evidence.ref: PR #583 diff excerpt: import_c_file conditionally inserted 'wine' at the start of the MWCC command when platform.system() == 'Linux'

statement: Build configuration should use a positive matching predicate such as MUST_MATCH for code-generation constraints; compiler or platform predicates such as MWERKS_GEKKO should independently guard target-specific syntax and must not be inferred from the absence of NON_MATCHING.

evidence.ref: PR #654 diff: Makefile adds -DMUST_MATCH and --defsym MUST_MATCH=1 only for matching builds
PR #654 diff: src/MetroTRK/mem_TRK.h and Runtime sources use MWERKS_GEKKO for compiler/platform-specific declarations
PR #654 review feedback: MUST_MATCH versus NON_MATCHING

statement: When a function uses inline assembly or object post-processing only because of compiler code generation, re-test its existing C implementation after changing compiler variants; MWCC 1.2.5n allowed the normal C implementations of gmMainLib_8015D084, gmMainLib_8015D450, it_8026B924, it_8026B960, and HSD_LObjGetCurrentByType to replace their MUST_MATCH assembly fallbacks.

corroboration.reason: PR #958 and the cited build report support retesting C implementations after compiler changes when assembly fallbacks existed for compiler-code-generation reasons.

corroboration.reason: The supplied PR and build-report evidence supports the scoped MetroTRK compiler-selection fact.

statement: When `NON_MATCHING` no longer affected source or matching behavior after removal of `MUST_MATCH`, it was removed together from the Makefile checksum logic, the normal CI matrix, and package-publishing validation; `SKIP_CHECK` remained the explicit checksum bypass and `GENERATE_MAP=1` remained a tested build mode.

corroboration.reason: This is a historical description of a completed removal rather than a reusable current-checkout lesson, and targeted PR search supplied no additional corroboration.

statement: A repository include-root migration must update every consumer of that topology together, including compiler and assembler flags, editor flags, formatting targets, context-generation scripts, generated-context locations, and affected source includes.

corroboration.reason: PR #666 supports coordinated updates across all consumers when repository include-root topology changes.

statement: A build configuration must not activate a compiler version until that compiler has been made available through the compiler archive and associated build environment.

evidence.ref: Oops, need to update the compiler zip + base docker image first.

corroboration.reason: The review feedback and PR ordering support provisioning a compiler in the archive and build environment before activating it in build configuration.

statement: Generated map files are the preferable source for function addresses during debugging and mod-tool integration: Dolphin, IDA, and Ghidra can load them, and tools can resolve function names to current addresses from the map. Requiring duplicated RAM or DOL address comments adds readability, maintenance, version-support, and PR-review costs.

A map-file parser intended for decompilation analysis should preserve local address, global address, size, alignment, symbol and parent names, and translation-unit association in an explicitly ordered output schema.

When CI reports that previously matched functions became broken after type work, investigate both changed struct layouts and changed function signatures because either can alter existing code generation.

evidence.ref: PR 1402 review comment by ribbanya: "It means they no longer match. Probably a struct change somewhere."
PR 1402 review comment by ribbanya: "Could also be a function signature change."

statement: When a group of float-looking loads and stores uses integer transfer instructions, test whether the source was an aggregate such as Vec3 and express it as a whole-struct assignment rather than independent member assignments.

If a function cannot yet be made exact, keep the normal build on the original assembly and place the documented C reconstruction behind the project's nonmatching configuration as a last resort; near-matches must not silently replace exact code.

A matched translation unit requires every function and its data to match. For an unmatched unit, the build system can use the original DOL content for final hash checking while retaining per-function percentages for regression comparisons.

During initial matching, postpone automatic style normalization and keep superficially cosmetic source permutations available: constructs such as braces around a single statement can change register allocation and generated code.

Preserve unresolved matching constraints as Doxygen-visible @todo entries adjacent to the affected symbol; for example, Camera_8002BD88 records that sharing the apparent x/y logic changes stack allocation, and fn_ToggleItemCollisionBubbles records an auto-inlining constraint.

subject.area: matching PR intake and regression triage

statement: Do not classify locally claimed function matches as safe progress until they are reconciled with available automated regression output; PR #2333 claimed five 100% matches while its bot report showed an overall matched-code decrease, 62 broken matches, and one unmatched-item regression.

evidence.ref: pr-2333 human_pr_text: Matched table claims five 100% matches in ftKb_SpecialN.c
pr-2333 text_corpus issue_comment: decomp-dev[bot] reports matched code -0.20% / -7728 bytes, 62 broken matches, and one unmatched-item regression

statement: Keep artificial stack slots, duplicate assignments, forced-active data, and no-inline controls explicitly annotated and confined to MUST_MATCH branches so matching requirements remain distinguishable from ordinary source logic.
Do not use register keywords or optimizer pragmas as ordinary matching controls; PR #2583 review required their removal from the affected fighter and game-mode sources.

If a clean checkout produces a nonmatching binary, treat the exact toolchain version as an experimental variable: reproduce with the same environment and test a known earlier version. In this incident, downgrading devkitPPC from r40-3 to r39 restored an OK build, although the batch did not establish the underlying cause or prove that r40-3 fails in every environment.

When refactoring matching C around a suspected shared pattern, first test the pattern on two or three very small representative functions in separate scratches, then expand it only if one formulation works across the set; small functions reduce the number of code-generation permutations.
Artificial stack padding and forced-active unused data needed only for exact matching should be isolated under MUST_MATCH and represented as byte storage when no semantic type is known.

Keep unavoidable matching artifacts isolated and explicit: compiler-specific inline assembly may coexist with a readable C path, and stack-shape padding should be guarded by MUST_MATCH rather than presented as gameplay logic.
Preserve source constructs needed only for matching, such as unused stack allocations and compiler-specific pragmas, behind `MUST_MATCH` so host tooling does not inherit matching-only behavior.

When exact output requires suspicious assignments, inline assembly, pragmas, or compiler-bug triggers, isolate that construct under MUST_MATCH and provide a readable portable implementation in the alternate branch.

evidence.ref: PR #654 diff: src/MSL/trigf.c keeps matching inline assembly under MUST_MATCH and C implementations under else branches

PR #654 diff: ftGameWatch_SpecialN_CreateSausage selects matching assembly versus a documented non-matching C implementation

statement: The normal matching-progress metric counts fully matched functions, while fuzzy progress measures matching bytes; a nearly matched function contributes to fuzzy progress but not to the normal function count.

corroboration.reason: This is the stronger base phrasing for the subject and is retained in a merged external-reference proposal that also incorporates the 100% fuzzy clarification.

statement: A 100% fuzzy score necessarily implies a complete byte match rather than merely a high partial-match score.

corroboration.reason: Its useful clarification is subsumed by the merged proposal based on the stronger companion learning, so retaining it independently would duplicate the same metrics subject.

statement: For matching-sensitive code, prefer typed struct access, but do not accept a large match regression merely to eliminate existing raw pointer arithmetic. If the clean form changes register allocation substantially, retain the matching pointer form as an explicit code-generation compromise and revisit it with better type or source-shape evidence.
Register replacement objects at the original ranges' build-order positions when splitting assembly; file relocation and object-list ordering must be changed together to preserve binary layout.
The Melee project targets NTSC version 1.02, also referred to in the discussion as 1.2 or Revision 2; support for earlier revisions was deferred.

After branch or split changes, stale build artifacts can produce misleading linkage and control-flow failures. If an incremental clean is insufficient, remove build/GALE01 or the full build directory before rebuilding; the full directory removal is the reliable clean-build fallback, while retaining downloaded tools may make removal of only build/GALE01 preferable.
For matching decompilation work, executing the rebuilt game is not required to verify instruction identity when the build's hash comparison succeeds.
A reported full-compilation test with GC CodeWarrior 1.0 exhibited the fixed epilogue scheduling described by that compiler's release notes.

corroboration.reason: The two cited messages consistently describe the reported GC CodeWarrior 1.0 full-compilation observation, subject to external-reference owner verification.

statement: GC CodeWarrior 1.0 and 1.1 both identify as compiler version 2.3.3 but are distinct builds: GC CW 1.0 is build 144 with an April 13, 2000 runtime, while GC CW 1.1 is build 159 with a February 7, 2001 runtime.

corroboration.reason: The cited message supports the precise distinction between the two compiler builds, but the external toolchain identity claim requires source-owner verification.

statement: Mac PPC CodeWarrior 2.2 was reported to produce strong instruction-body similarity to the sought Melee compiler, with the principal observed differences in EABI prologue and epilogue generation.

corroboration.reason: A single reported similarity observation with lower confidence does not establish a stable compiler-identification fact or reusable matching rule.

statement: For an unfamiliar translation unit, start with functions and define data as code requires it, then finish matching data afterward. Correct section placement still matters because sections such as `.sdata2` and `.data` produce different code generation.

Once referenced data is identified, split and type it rather than leaving it represented by raw section offsets or extern placeholders; accurate ownership and linkage can be necessary for the surrounding code to match.

When an unavailable or behaviorally incompatible compiler prevents some functions from matching, decompilation can continue by retaining assembly for those nonmatching functions while converting functions that do match.

A rebuilt Melee boot.dol cannot generally run in isolation because it loads assets from the game disc; test it with an extracted game filesystem by replacing the extracted DOL with the build output, or configure the original game as Dolphin's Default Game so it supplies the current disc context.

subject.area: melee ft and lb module naming

statement: For assembly partitioning under the melee ft and lb areas, use a semantic module filename when module identity is supported, while retaining an address-derived filename for an unidentified residual range.

Attribute expression-shape or folded/propagated-value mismatches to the frontend IR optimizer; missing/extra CSE or hoisted loop values to the backend optimizer sequence; instruction-order-only differences to scheduling or peephole; register-identity-only differences to coalescing roots or select order; stack offsets/frame size to memory-homing and frame regions; and the `stmw` start or saved-register span to select order or peak pressure through the lowest claimed callee-saved register. See `games/melee/knowledge/sources/rag_search/mwcc_compiler_notes/data/mwcc-compiler-notes.md` for full detail.

Stop source-shape register sweeps when the residual is a terminal callee-saved permutation among compiler-materialized webs with no nameable local owner, an extra-callee-saved/peak-pressure mismatch caused by one extra live value, or a many-to-many reallocation in which one candidate register maps to several retail registers across regions. These respectively reflect unreachable equal-cost web ordering, an upstream frontend-lowering difference with cascading assignments, or a wholesale different select history rather than a clean source-steerable rotation; see `games/melee/knowledge/sources/rag_search/mwcc_compiler_notes/data/mwcc-compiler-notes.md` for full detail.

Under the reported MWCC 1.1 configuration, merely introducing the asm keyword in a translation unit could alter prologue generation in other functions; a nonmatching or assembly-injection mechanism should avoid adding asm to a translation unit whose surrounding functions must retain matching code generation.

For MWCC permutation runs, normalize or exclude known standalone-compilation artifacts from scoring instead of compiling every candidate through an additional cleanup pass: MWCC 1.2.5e emitted a trailing __PROFILE_EXIT call and nop, Frank removed them, and later directly ignoring the affected epilogue lines avoided the extra compile and improved throughput.
With MWCC, introducing a nested block lets declarations be moved nearer their uses; this can alter register allocation, and the block is necessary because declarations must occur at a block start.

statement: In MWCC matching, local-variable declaration order can alter register allocation; swapping declarations is a targeted tactic for an otherwise isolated register swap.

statement: MWCC GC/1.2.5 uses a Chaitin-style graph-coloring allocator with Briggs-style optimistic coloring and aggressive Chaitin-style coalescing: each non-interfering copy-related pair merges, with the lower-numbered web surviving. Spill cost is `cost += block_weight × (2 if definition, 1 if use, 3 if both)` per operand, simplify removes degree-below-color-count nodes then the lowest `spill_cost / degree` node, and equal-degree/equal-cost ties follow list dynamics over virtual-register numbering; select takes the lowest available color bit, with GPR `{r0, r3..r12}` and FPR `{f0..f13}` initially available and callee-saved colors claimed on demand high-to-low (`r31..r14`, `f31..f14`). See `games/melee/knowledge/sources/rag_search/mwcc_compiler_notes/data/mwcc-compiler-notes.md` for full detail.

Proven source-level register-assignment levers in MWCC GC/1.2.5 are initializer-bearing pointer locals, declaration order of long-lived locals, splitting a reused local into mutually exclusive variables, one-field aggregate wrappers, changing scalar type width, and declaration-with-initializer versus separate assignment; each can alter coalescing roots, virtual-register creation, rank, or simplify/select order even when emitted values are equivalent. The `register` keyword was byte-neutral at `-O4,p` in tested cases. See `games/melee/knowledge/sources/rag_search/mwcc_compiler_notes/data/mwcc-compiler-notes.md` for full detail.

When a function differs only in register allocation, test local declaration order and source-statement order, including statements optimized out of the final assembly; both can alter MWCC allocation without changing runtime behavior.

id: learning:area:static data layout and translation-unit splitting:b32fb3900bb13b1a

subject.area: static data layout and translation-unit splitting

statement: Matching static data requires preserving declaration order, output section, const qualification, and initialization form; translation-unit boundaries also matter because constants that can be shared within one file may be emitted separately after a file split.

Clang-query is useful for prototyping decomp CI checks before implementing a permanent matcher. Use IgnoreUnlessSpelledInSource to reduce generated-code noise, but account for preprocessing: macro names such as JOBJ_HIDDEN disappear, so checks may need to recognize the resulting typed expression shape and explicitly refine known false positives.

File-owned BSS or data should have one definition in its owning C file and should be exposed through a header only when cross-translation-unit references require external linkage; an extern declaration does not substitute for deciding ownership.

Use a module static header for file-local data layouts and translation-unit-specific matching helpers, while retaining offset-derived names and comments where semantics remain uncertain; gmallstar.static.h, gmregtyfall.static.h, and grbigblue.static.h demonstrate this boundary.
Under CodeWarrior -requireprotos, write no-argument functions with an explicit (void) parameter list in both declarations and definitions; foo() is not a strict C prototype.

statement: Use ordinary inline string literals for source-level string arguments rather than representing compiler-combined string tables as offset expressions or generated data symbols, unless separate data-ownership evidence requires otherwise.

When a stubborn register-allocation mismatch remains, test whether contiguous fields were represented incorrectly as separate members rather than an array; participants reported an IDO mismatch that occurred in only one function and was resolved by changing the members to an array.

When recovering a struct from another project, retain only fields supported by current code and preserve visible offsets for unresolved layout-sensitive members; unsupported copied fields create misleading layout assumptions.

Offset prefixes in structure-member names are useful as a temporary assembly-comparison aid, but once a member's purpose is known, prefer a semantic name and preserve the offset in a declaration comment or tooling rather than in the identifier.

M2C_FIELD can be used as a temporary matching aid, but proper typed fields are preferable because M2C_FIELD may affect code generation and does not propagate recovered structure information to other functions.

corroboration.reason: This is substantively covered by the accepted typed-fields-over-pointer-math standard, which more strongly states that M2C_FIELD may not ship when a real type can express the access.

statement: When only part of a large structure is understood, represent unknown ranges as filler and split out fields only when access offsets and usage establish their types; this avoids prematurely propagating many speculative fields.

corroboration.reason: The two human-source comments consistently support retaining filler for unproven ranges and exposing fields only when offsets and usage establish their types.

statement: The Infinite Super Scope glitch occurs because an exhausted charged-shot case returns the scope object's pointer as a negative charge level; when a hit interrupts charging, subtracting that negative level from ammo adds roughly 2.1 billion shots.

Accept semantic renames and field names only after behavior has been reasonably validated, such as with the Dolphin debugger, manual in-game checks, or equivalent direct evidence. Inferred names without behavioral investigation can mislead later work even when they follow naming style.
Treat community symbol-map names as hypotheses: verify a proposed name against the decompiled behavior and surrounding subsystem before applying it.

statement: Complex AI-generated symbol names require manual review and should document which model produced them; simple getter and setter names remain acceptable only after manual review and should be grounded in existing codebase names such as field names.

corroboration.reason: The review discussion supports manual review, model provenance, and local grounding for AI-generated symbol names; this remains a standards-owner proposal.

statement: Treat community or Dolphin-derived symbol maps as cross-reference material rather than automatically renaming unresolved functions: the batch reports verifiably incorrect and misleading names, while address-based placeholders remain stable for lookup until behavior is established.

corroboration.reason: The accepted infer-authored-source-style standard already establishes that external maps and generated suggestions cannot outrank matched local source and headers.

statement: Do not treat an inherited semantic function name as evidence of behavior; understand the function through matching or other local evidence before assigning such a name.
For large symbol migrations, derive address-keyed old-to-new pairs by comparing linker maps, then apply the reviewed replacement list separately.

statement: For repository-wide symbol renames, use `melee-replace-symbols` rather than ad hoc editor or sed substitutions, then compare an upstream-master `ninja baseline` against a branch `ninja changes`; ordinary builds can succeed despite incomplete implementation renames, and name-based progress reports can misleadingly show renamed symbols as removed.

The SysDolphin object model uses class metadata containing lifecycle callbacks such as allocation, initialization, release, destruction, and amnesia; its higher-level Object abstraction adds reference counting to that class mechanism.

In the reported MWCC 1.1 sysdolphin matching case, per-function scheduling pragmas remained ineffective even with push/pop, and separating inline assembly into another assembly object did not resolve the epilogue mismatch; pragma-based scheduling should therefore be validated against a minimal reproducer before being adopted as a fix.

statement: Do not change a shared structure's type or size merely to absorb a linker-section discrepancy. First compare all users and versioned layouts, determine whether the unexplained bytes are accessed, and investigate section ownership, split boundaries, and alignment independently.

Do not batch-apply Sysdolphin names from external public symbol maps without verification; the batch reports known inaccuracies in those maps. MetroTRK version strings are not reliable proxies for compiler version or matching code generation: the batch distinguishes separate Dolphin and GameCube MetroTRK version lines and reports that other sysdolphin binaries with comparable MetroTRK versions still use different epilogue ordering.
When choosing between easy progress and foundational work, Sysdolphin functions can be higher leverage because matching them exposes behavior and context useful for matching other subsystems.

For the tested MWCC compiler, deferred inlining postpones inlining until all functions have been compiled, permitting calls to be inlined even when their definitions occur later in the translation unit. Smart inlining performs multiple passes and restricts later passes to small functions.

Do not assume enum-backed fields can be converted to smaller enum types without affecting matching or structure layout: the investigated MWCC interface exposed `-enum int` and `-enum min`, and `-enum min` did not match, so such changes require match and layout verification rather than a mechanical type replacement.
Before attributing a code-generation difference to the compiler executable or hotfix version, verify the complete compiler flags; a stray debug flag such as `-g` can produce the apparent difference.

When target assembly contains an apparently unnecessary temporary struct copy, test a C compound-literal assignment: an expression such as myVec = (Vec){...} can materialize a temporary on the stack and then copy it into the destination.

A C declaration tells the compiler a symbol exists; resolution against other object files is the linker's responsibility. An unused extern declaration does not require resolution, so an invalid extern name only produces an undefined-symbol error once retained code references it.

Mirrored match gains and losses under old and new unit paths should be treated as rename accounting rather than semantic matching progress when the address ranges and source bodies were moved together.
Broken-match counts assigned to a deleted translation unit during a file split are not sufficient evidence of a regression; compare replacement-unit matches and net matched and linked byte deltas.

corroboration.reason: The cited discussion supports frequent incremental submission and releasing claims that will remain blocked for an extended period.

statement: For repository work, create each feature branch from an up-to-date branch tracking upstream master, submit the pull request from that feature branch, and delete it after merge; keeping changes off the fork's master avoids unnecessary divergence, and new work can be based directly on upstream master without synchronizing the fork's master.

When equivalent source was built for both PPC and x86 by the same compiler family, the x86 output could disambiguate source control flow: PPC consistently branched to an epilogue for returns, while x86 returned immediately, revealing whether an explicit `return` existed or control merely reached the end of a block.
Prefer ordinary include guards over MWCC's -once option when headers must remain compatible with GCC and other modern compilers.

A 100% MWCC PowerPC match establishes reproduction of the target object under that toolchain, but does not by itself guarantee equivalent behavior when the C is compiled with another compiler or architecture; undefined behavior, uninitialized data, floating-point rounding, and compiler code generation require separate runtime validation.

For compiler code intended to run on modern hosts, use fixed-width or semantic integer types where width matters instead of assuming `long` is 32 bits; the historical CodeWarrior plugin headers used `long` for 32-bit values, which is not portable to every modern ABI.

Persist concrete past matching attempts, including what worked, what failed, and why; this history can keep agents from repeating abandoned tactics and can supply relevant precedents when they become stuck.

Broad matching branches should be split or have valid matches extracted before prolonged drift: PR #2238 touched 71 files and was closed unmerged after maintainers reported that its conflicts required impractical manual resolution and later drift made merging impossible.

corroboration.reason: The general anchor exists, and the evidence supports isolated decomp.me scratches for parallel work and reduced source-branch conflicts.

statement: When decompilation work stalls after some functions are complete, publish the work on a visible branch or WIP PR so others can review and continue it; do not leave completed matches only in decomp.me or a private working tree for weeks.

corroboration.reason: The general anchor exists, and the evidence independently supports publishing stalled completed work so collaborators can review and continue it.

statement: Documentation for tasks such as source splitting should provide concrete examples and rules of thumb while acknowledging that decompilation rarely has one universally correct procedure.

A simple register swap in nonmatching output is potentially behavior-neutral only after checking that the swapped values do not escape the function, that calls obey the ABI, and that no undefined behavior invalidates those assumptions; closer matching makes that assessment more reliable.

Incremental matching work can be integrated once the retained functions are complete, but do not fragment a translation unit into many artificial C/assembly pieces solely to select isolated functions; excessive splitting creates merge and maintenance overhead.

Treat decomp.me output as an iteration aid rather than final proof for inlining-sensitive matches: compilation-unit treatment and linker optimizations can make its output differ from the repository's full build, so validate the result in the full build.
Fork a shared decomp.me scratch before modifying it when the original nonmatching state and the sequence of changes may be useful for review or learning.
Before investigating an unexpected compiler diff, synchronize the local source with the current decomp.me scratch source so the comparison is based on identical code.

Use a one-function decomp.me scratch while matching because including several functions complicates iteration; integrate the functions into the live source together when the containing translation unit is ready.
Set the decomp.me diff target to the exact attempted function name. If it does not match, diff.py may compare the whole file and display unrelated lines.

statement: For reviewable decomp.me scratches, move declarations that may need editing—such as a relevant class or struct definition—into the source tab instead of leaving them buried in a large context.

corroboration.reason: The general anchor exists, and the evidence supports placing editable declarations in the scratch source tab for reviewability.

statement: A decomp.me scratch is normally scoped to one function: paste that function's assembly, select the Melee preset for the expected compiler settings, and provide context when the function needs project headers, typedefs, or declarations.

A decomp.me target generally needs only the function label and instruction body; remove surrounding macros.inc directives. Include the relevant data section when the function references data required for assembly, especially a jump table.

To investigate a recurring code-generation mismatch, first find the smallest functions that still exhibit it and use them as focused test cases. Reducing the function size removes unrelated variables and narrows the plausible source-level permutations.

Do not treat a decomp.me similarity percentage as a monotonic measure of correctness: a semantically and structurally improved candidate can temporarily score lower, and operand order, arithmetic direction, or unequal floating constants can explain why a superficially higher-scoring candidate is still wrong.

Use other decompilation projects only as references; independently validate declarations and behavior rather than copying them, because copied assumptions can propagate incorrect types or structure layouts.

Use permutation search primarily to finish functions that are already very close to matching; it is effective for that final stage but does not replace the larger semantic and structural portion of decompilation work.

When investigating a suspected inline in a nonmatching function, move local declarations into the narrowest plausible scope, using explicit scope braces if needed; changes in register allocation or code shape can reveal the likely inline boundary.

Within a translation unit, decompiling small functions first is efficient because they may reveal inlines used by larger functions, and simple accessors help establish structure layouts. Beginner suitability depends more on repeated, rigid patterns than on instruction count alone.
After learning basic C, perturb already matched functions and compare the generated assembly to learn which C syntax and source patterns MWCC selects.

Melee matching work aims to reconstruct C that compiles to the exact assembly in the original binary; hand translation of assembly and decompiler output are complementary inputs rather than authoritative source.

corroboration.reason: The general anchor exists, and the statement consistently distinguishes exact binary matching from non-authoritative translation and decompiler inputs.

statement: For translation-unit data matching, verify with a local linked build and objdiff rather than relying only on decomp.me: decomp.me does not expose all data sections and requires careful manual tracking of context changes.

corroboration.reason: The general anchor exists, and the cited attempts support linked-build and objdiff verification for translation-unit data not fully represented by decomp.me.

statement: A low-confusion workflow for converting an assembly translation unit is to match one function at a time, moving each matched function from the top of the assembly file into its C file; extern data can alter code generation and require additional adjustment.

corroboration.reason: The general anchor exists, and the evidence supports function-by-function translation-unit conversion together with the caveat that extern data can affect code generation.

statement: Treat m2c output as a starting point: first replace invalid or unknown declarations so the C compiles, then correct inferred types and iterate on the remaining assembly differences.

corroboration.reason: The general anchor exists, and the attempts support treating m2c output as a staged starting point rather than authoritative source.

statement: AI-cleaned pseudocode should be treated as a starting point rather than evidence of a match: it can simplify a function and accelerate manual work, but exact matching output was reported as rare and incorrect output still required manual correction.

corroboration.reason: The general anchor exists, and the evidence supports treating AI-cleaned pseudocode as an aid rather than evidence of an exact match.

statement: When triaging unmatched assembly, starting with the smallest units or functions helps build familiarity with recurring compiler patterns before tackling larger ones.

corroboration.reason: The general anchor exists, and the evidence supports smallest-first triage as distinct workflow guidance for learning compiler patterns.

statement: Matching decompiler output is not sufficient source quality when it retains type-erasing casts or byte-offset pointer arithmetic; recover typed fields, union arms, or accessors before treating the source as finished.
A locally cached Docker image tagged `latest` may be reused without checking for a newer remote image; explicitly pull the image when a build starts requiring newly added compiler files.

Before classifying non-byte-identical code as functionally equivalent, exercise the rebuilt function in a modified DOL: instrument it with OSReport and verify expected values and timing, or temporarily remove its body and confirm that the relevant game behavior breaks. Minor register swaps can be compatible with equivalence, but an untested function is not evidence of equivalence.

For floating constants in matching C, test a direct typed literal such as 1.0 or 1.0f rather than assuming an external data symbol; both literal versus extern representation and extern versus extern const can change code generation.

For an unmatched function, use m2c output only as a starting point, eliminate large structural differences first, then iterate semantically equivalent C forms and introduce or move temporaries to tune load timing and register allocation.

corroboration.reason: Combines structural-first matching with targeted temporary placement and register-allocation iteration; it is more comprehensive than a generic m2c warning.

statement: Use decomp-permuter after a function is already close to matching; it can search small source-level variations such as declaration and expression ordering that are tedious to enumerate manually.

corroboration.reason: Duplicate of the stronger late-stage decomp-permuter formulation in learning:general:matching workflow:a6aa4f0f14299303, which additionally records the semantic-quality risk.

statement: Use objdiff for routine local comparison, and move a function to decomp.me when it is difficult to match by inspection or needs to be shared for outside help.
A target-exact checkpoint with failed hard gates is only partial progress, not a successful retained decompilation change; same-unit regressions and QA failures must be repaired before selection.
A closed, unmerged PR whose available record contains only its body and no diff should be treated as evidence of proposal intent, not as evidence that the described behavior exists in the repository.
A raw target-score improvement is not retainable when the checkpoint fails the same-unit-regression or QA hard gate; validation status and gates override the score increase.
An exact checkdiff result is insufficient to make a worker checkpoint selectable when the QA lint hard gate fails.

Ghidra's assembly and decompiler views can be highlighted in either direction to locate corresponding code; correspondence may resolve only to a whole decompiled statement rather than a specific subexpression.
In Ghidra, undefined4 means only that the value has an unknown four-byte type; it does not establish that the value is an int or any other specific C type.

After a pull request is squash-merged, Git treats the squashed upstream commit as distinct from the original branch commits. Consequently, a three-dot comparison can misleadingly show already-integrated branch commits, while a two-dot comparison checks the endpoint trees directly; rebasing preserves local work but may require conflict resolution.

When a formatting-heavy header change conflicts with concurrent semantic edits, start from the reformatted current header and reapply the semantic changes rather than resolving the combined diff through GitHub's merge UI; verify the result with an independent local merge before accepting it.

A formatting-only PR can establish mechanical style context, but without semantic edits, review rationale, or validation output it does not support conclusions about symbol meaning, matching tactics, or decomp correctness.

statement: When targeting a specific PowerPC instruction form or register ordering, search the project's assembly for the same opcode and operand pattern and inspect the corresponding C. For example, compound assignment such as `*=` can encourage `fmuls f1, f1, f0`.

Do not introduce an i32, x32, or unk32 typedef to conceal unknown signedness: inspect comparisons and load instructions for evidence, use a comment while uncertainty remains, and use int when no explicit fixed-width intent is indicated.

A set of individually 100%-matched functions is not sufficient to establish correct linked runtime behavior. Linking can expose wrong symbol references or constants, and fakematches containing undefined or layout-dependent accesses may stop working when data or translation units shift; runtime testing remains necessary.

Project shiftability depends on references being represented as linker-resolved symbol relocations rather than embedded absolute addresses; it is not determined by the percentage of code already decompiled.

After making M2C output compile, simplify or eliminate generated temporaries before fine-grained matching; the temporary-heavy output can obscure the source-level expression structure and associated compiler patterns.

If m2c fails while parsing generated context at a preprocessor directive and the installed revision is stale, compare the installed commit with a working environment; in the reported case pip upgrade commands did not replace the old Git installation, but uninstalling and reinstalling m2c resolved the problem.

An M2C_FIELD access should be translated into a typed structure field at the encoded byte offset. For example, M2C_FIELD(arg0, s32*, 4) represents an s32 field at offset 4, with padding or preceding members accounting for the first four bytes.

Provide first-pass m2c output when using an LLM for decompilation. For large functions, trying m2c with --gotos-only can produce a high-completion control-flow skeleton that can then be refactored incrementally into normal structured C while repeatedly preserving the match.

Generated context files should be written with an explicit UTF-8 encoding rather than the platform default, which was UTF-8 on Linux but an ANSI encoding on Windows and caused cross-platform decoding problems.

A function-level decomp.me match verifies the generated code under the selected compiler context, but submission still requires checking the translation unit's data sections and the repository's final DOL checksum.

A 100% fuzzy match does not necessarily establish a perfect linked match: objdiff's fuzzy or relocation-insensitive mode can ignore exact data offsets, so inspect the perfect-match and fully-linked categories when assessing project progress.

Function definition order within a source file ultimately matters for a matching linked object, but an ordering mistake is not immediately consequential while the file remains unlinked. Header inclusion and agreement between the source and header signatures should still be checked when adding a matched definition.

After a matching-DOL result, deliberately make a small known output-changing edit and verify that the comparison fails. This confirms that the build and comparison are consuming the edited source rather than stale output.

An exact byte match proves that the current compiler invocation produced the target bytes, but does not prove that the recovered C is the original source or that equivalent future source edits will compile identically; matching must therefore be reviewed alongside source plausibility and behavior.

An assembly match establishes only that the candidate belongs to the set of source forms producing that output; prefer explanations that remain consistent across related functions, while allowing genuine inconsistencies caused by later edits or different authors.

statement: Matching assembly establishes equivalence of the emitted machine instructions, but it does not uniquely recover source-level context such as names, aggregate layout, or whether a word-sized operation originated from one u32 or several adjacent u8 fields.

corroboration.reason: This is the strongest and most concrete formulation of the subject's source-nonuniqueness limitation.

statement: When testing whether a helper, macro, or inline is required for matching, begin with the smallest function whose match depends on it so the code-generation effect is isolated.

Use decomp-permuter after a function is already close to matching; its randomized C transformations are most useful for residual register-allocation differences or a final small mismatch, not as a substitute for constructing the function.

Use decomp-permuter mainly as a late-stage diagnostic for register or instruction swaps, and review its output critically because it can obtain a match by inserting semantically empty, unnatural source that merely perturbs register allocation.

corroboration.reason: The general anchor exists, and the evidence supports both late-stage diagnostic use of decomp-permuter and critical review of unnatural matching output.

statement: When starting from decompiler output, first restore functional equivalence, then remove unnecessary temporaries and reduce the function to minimal C; only reintroduce temporaries or alternate equivalent expressions as needed before trying manual or automated permutations.

corroboration.reason: The general anchor exists, and the evidence supports restoring equivalence and simplifying decompiler-derived source before introducing matching-sensitive variants.

statement: A decompilation is a match only when compilation and linking reproduce the target instruction bytes exactly; differing assembler-local branch or literal labels do not invalidate a match when the emitted bytes are identical.
For a mechanical source transformation, record the exact search/replacement expression and explicitly delimit excluded cases so reviewers can reproduce and audit its scope.

statement: When investigating an apparent Metrowerks inline, prioritize definitions visible in the same translation unit during preprocessing; inlining a separately compiled translation unit would require link-time optimization.
Metrowerks linker-map parsers must account for linker-version-dependent column layouts: older linker output may omit the File Offset column.
After applying a byte-level compiler or linker patch, verify the resulting byte at the intended offset or compare a checksum; a dd command can complete without producing the intended patched binary.

In Metrowerks matching, exact signedness and type structure must be established across all uses: a type that matches almost everywhere as u32 but fails in one function may instead be int, and the distinction should be proven through matching.

When reconstructing an MWCC loop, repeated expressions derived from the induction variable may be strength-reduced into incremented offset temporaries; different byte strides can produce multiple temporaries.

corroboration.reason: The general anchor exists, and the evidence consistently supports MWCC strength reduction of induction-variable expressions into incremented offset temporaries.

statement: Do not assume logically equivalent C expressions produce identical MWCC output; even forms such as x = x + 1, x++, and x += 1 can alter code generation, so expression spelling remains a valid matching variable.

corroboration.reason: The general anchor exists, and the evidence supports expression spelling as an independent MWCC code-generation variable.

statement: Long chain-assignment shape or ordering can alter MWCC code generation hundreds of lines away without visibly changing all intervening code; when manual edits cannot localize such a mismatch, a targeted chain-assignment randomization pass can expose it.

For MWCC near-matches, algebraically equivalent expressions can produce different common-subexpression elimination, temporary lifetimes, register assignments, stack positions, and operand ordering; test both repeated expression shapes and deliberately different equivalent forms.
For MWCC enum matching, otherwise-unused enumerators can influence the enum's representation; in particular, adding a negative enumerator forces a signed representation.
Do not change MWCC inlining settings globally merely to match one function, because that can break other matches; localize forced inlining with a push/pop-scoped `#pragma always_inline on` region.

When investigating an MWCC loop expected to emit subfic/cmpwi/bge, make the loop's initial value a non-constant expression. Use #pragma ppc_unroll_instructions_limit 1 to inspect the underlying loop shape without unrolling, but treat the pragma as a diagnostic rather than a universal matching fix.

When diagnosing MWCC stack or register mismatches, vary source shape rather than only semantics: inline-local versus parent-local placement can change stack layout, while register allocation is sensitive to live ranges, declaration order, types, and even equivalent spellings such as ++ and += 1.

In the MWCC O4,p experiments recorded in this batch, a loop containing a remaining function call did not unroll, whereas an inline call that disappeared during optimization did not by itself prevent unrolling; exact trip-count limits should be re-tested for the compiler version, language mode, and loop body.

Treat MWCC register allocation as a whole-function property: small source changes can alter virtual-register scores and cause cascading allocation changes, so local instruction fixes must be evaluated against the complete function diff.

MWCC's top-down encounter order for function bodies and definitions, including inline functions, can affect floating-point constant ordering in small-data sections; definition placement should therefore be checked when otherwise matched text has an sdata2 ordering mismatch.

Double-precision constants require 8-byte alignment, so a 32-bit padding word between a float and a following double can be intentional. Raw disassembly may show that padding as unexplained data, but a typed C definition should reproduce the alignment automatically.
For GameCube and Wii analysis, the relevant calling convention is the PowerPC Embedded ABI; assembly rN denotes general-purpose register N, while fN denotes floating-point register N.
Opcode-analysis tooling can run a preprocessing pass that recognizes known multi-instruction idioms from distinctive opcodes, constants, or call arguments before its main translation pass.

In PowerPC disassembly, an instruction mnemonic suffixed with '.' records the operation result into the condition register, while '+' and '-' on conditional branches encode static likely and unlikely prediction hints.

Under the PowerPC EABI, r2 supplies the base for .sdata2 references and r13 supplies the base for the .sdata/.sbss area. In an unlinked scratch, an external small-data reference may display with base 0 instead of r2; that relocation difference can still become correct in the linked build.

On PowerPC, stfs to a stack slot followed by lwz from that slot transfers the float's full 32-bit representation into a GPR; it is bit reinterpretation, not a numeric float-to-integer conversion. A later lfs from the same slot may also force single-precision rounding.
PowerPC `fctiwz` converts a floating-point operand to a 32-bit signed integer using round-toward-zero semantics and places the integer in the low word of the destination floating-point register.

statement: For PowerPC instructions such as rlwinm, the dotted record form updates the condition register; therefore rlwinm and rlwinm. are behaviorally distinct even when their destination-register results are otherwise identical.

statement: For the common PowerPC integer-to-double conversion constant beginning with 0x43300000, a zero low word corresponds to the unsigned conversion path, while a 0x80000000 low word corresponds to the signed conversion path.

For PowerPC integer-to-floating-point conversion sequences, the generated 0x4330000000000000 versus 0x4330000080000000 bias constant depends on whether the converted integer is unsigned or signed; an unexpected sdata2 constant should therefore prompt a signedness check.

PowerPC address relocations split or relativize addresses: @ha and @l support reconstructing an address with high-adjusted and low portions, while @sda21 addresses data relative to the fixed small-data bases associated with r2 or r13 so nearby objects can be accessed with one instruction.

In decomp.me comparisons, a target instruction using r2 or r13 may appear as a generated instruction using base register 0 because decomp.me has not applied the final linker relocation; this is especially common for lfs and lfd and should not be treated as a C-code mismatch by itself.

When diagnosing an uncertain function signature, inspect whether incoming argument registers are read before being overwritten, inspect the final value written to the ABI return register, and inspect callers for immediate use of that register; an incorrect or missing parameter or return declaration can also manifest as an m2c unset-register error.

At a PowerPC variadic call site, crclr 6 indicates that none of the variadic arguments is floating-point, while crset 6 indicates that at least one is floating-point; the instruction is tied to the variadic calling convention, not inherently to text printing.
